source: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, MSL APXS calibrated oxide-abundance products (RDR, '*rwp*' tables)
licence: NASA Planetary Data System, public domain. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Guelph (APXS team)
units: weight percent, as written in each product (Ni, Zn and Br are also in weight percent, not ppm)
notes: One entry per APXS measurement (one oxide table). The same target can appear several times: before and after brushing (DRT), offsets, rasters, drill tailings and dump piles. Values are the product's abundance column; the product's statistical-uncertainty column is not carried. The archive warns that short, warm or distant measurements have poorer minor and trace elements. Target names are the science team's informal names, spelled as in the archive's activity tables. Any oxide table whose target is the rover's own APXS calibration target is left out (0 found in this build).
join_note: Each product name carries the sol, site and drive of the rover when the measurement was made (ap?_<clock>rwp<sol 4><site 3><drive 4>). site_drive is the stop id in data/site.json, so the join is exact; the spot itself is within arm's reach (about 2 m) of that rover position. The target name is joined through the unit letter and spacecraft clock of the raw file listed in extras/msl_apxs_activities_sol*.csv.
coverage_note: Sols 46 to 4842 (archive lists sols 46 to 4842). All listed oxide tables were read. 1 measurement(s) made at a site/drive that is not a stop in site.json are left out.
